messages.subject: Re: new "contributors" rather than "students"
messages.body_plain:
Also new is that there are two different project sizes, "Medium size projects should take about 175 hours to complete while large projects should take about 350 hours to complete."
https://developers.google.com/open-source/gsoc/faq#how_much_time_does_gsoc_participation_take
Stipend amounts now depend on project size, for example $3000 for medium and $6000 for large for contributors in USA. https://developers.google.com/open-source/gsoc/help/student-stipends#total_stipend_amount

On Monday, January 10, 2022 at 10:12:34 AM UTC-7 tdh...@gmail.com wrote:
> Hey all, I noticed that the new GSOC 22 guidelines/FAQ have been posted, and they have changed "students" to "contributors" so there is no longer a requirement about students being enrolled in university. instead the analogous requirement is that the contributor must be an open-source beginner (which I guess is our responsibility as mentors/admins to verify). https://developers.google.com/open-source/gsoc/faq#what_are_the_eligibility_requirements_for_participation
> There is still the rule that a contributor can only participate in at most 2 GSOCs. The official wording is: You have not been accepted as a GSoC Student in GSoC more than once. (Only GSoC Students from 2020 or 2021 are eligible to apply a second time in 2022.)
> https://developers.google.com/open-source/gsoc/faq#what_are_the_eligibility_requirements_for_participation

messages.subject: Re: new "contributors" rather than "students"
messages.body_plain:
Clicking on eligibility requirements link shows this:

——-
I attend a community college (or a junior college) can I still participate?

Yes, we hope you do! You just need to show the proof of enrollment in your college program.
——-

Which looks like there is still a student requirement.

Jeff
